author: Blog Staff
description:
Building on the previous article, Raymond Chen explores how deleted functions can produce clearer compiler errors when derived classes fail to implement required non-virtual methods. He also examines C++26’s new custom diagnostic messages for deleted functions, their compiler support, and why this technique works in C++/WinRT but not C++/WRL.

On forcing all derived classes to implement a specific non-virtual method, part 2

by Raymond Chen
